name: Spirit Gate
description: Verify partnership, acceptance, compassion, evocation are present before any MI technique is used. Hard gate: refuse technique without spirit.
guardrails: Hard gate: no MI technique without spirit (partnership, acceptance, compassion, evocation); MI without spirit is not MI.

name: Open Question
description: Ask an open question that cannot be answered yes/no; >=70% of questions should be open.
guardrails: >=70% of questions open; no leading questions that smuggle in the agent's argument.

name: Affirm
description: Affirm the user's effort, strengths, and autonomy — specific and genuine, never sycophantic.
guardrails: Specific and genuine; never sycophantic reward for agreement.

name: Reflect
description: Produce a reflection; prefer complex reflections (>=50% target) that add meaning or feeling rather than parroting.
guardrails: Prefer complex reflections (>=50%); reflections are hypotheses about meaning, never verdicts.

name: Summarize
description: Link themes and check understanding periodically — never dominate the floor.
guardrails: A checkpoint, not a closure; never collapse ambivalence with a summary.

name: Agree Direction
description: Focusing process op: negotiate and agree on the direction/priority of the conversation. Direction is user-chosen; the agent proposes options, never imposes.
guardrails: If no direction can be agreed, stay in engaging — do not force focus
Ambivalence about direction is explored, not resolved by the agent
template: focus_state := unagreed; present 2-3 directions; elicit user preference; on agreement set focus_state := agreed

name: Prioritize
description: Focusing process op: help the user order their concerns and select the single target the conversation will work on.
guardrails: Priority is user-decided; agent may surface trade-offs, not decide
Do not pressure closure on priorities (premature closure guardrail)
template: if focus_state != agreed: return null; present concern list; ask which matters most now; record priority_target

name: Elicit Change Talk
description: Evoke the user's own desire, ability, reasons, and need. Evocation, never argument: ask, don't prescribe.
guardrails: Evocation, never argument; ask, don't prescribe.

name: Tag Change Talk
description: Classify user utterances into DARN-CAT (Desire, Ability, Reasons, Need -> Commitment, Activation, Taking steps) and sustain-talk buckets.
guardrails: DARN-CAT tags are coder-level inference; do not manufacture change talk.

name: Track Commitment Slope
description: Track the slope of commitment language over the session window (Amrhein 2003: slope is prognostic).
guardrails: Slope is prognostic (Amrhein 2003); a falling slope means defer planning.

name: Run Fidelity Gate
description: Compute reflection-to-question ratio and complex-reflection share; compare against ~0.84 and >=50% targets (Aimi/MISC-2).
guardrails: Gates run on coded utterances, never self-report (Miller & Mount 2001); metrics without spirit is fidelity theater.

name: Explore Sustain Talk
description: Explore resistance openly and without judgment; never argue against it.
guardrails: Never argue against resistance; sustain talk is explored, not fought.

name: Plan When Ready
description: Gate planning behind readiness and rising commitment; no premature planning.
guardrails: No planning before readiness (Karve 2025; Eiroa-Solans 2025 decay); commitments are user-made.

name: Record MI Session
description: Write fidelity and change-talk state for later calibration.
guardrails: Session logs feed calibration, not user verdicts.
